title: Cathie Wood Swapped Nvidia for SpaceX Over the Risk of “Losing Jensen” to Musk. Oops.
html:
Cathie Wood Swapped Nvidia for SpaceX Over the Risk of “Losing Jensen” to Musk. Oops.

Key Takeaways

  • ARK Invest sold $85 million of Nvidia the day before its earnings report and put the money into SpaceX.

  • Cathie Wood says ARK sold because it could lose Jensen Huang to Elon Musk. Days later, Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as CEO.

  • Nvidia trades at 8.7x forward earnings, the lowest point in 10 years.

  • ARK sold near the lowest valuation in a decade over a risk that's now gone, and the delayed quarterly report is the bigger near-term test.

ARK Invest sold $85 million of Nvidia (NVDA:NASDAQ) the day before the chipmaker's earnings report and swapped the money into SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ).

On today's episode of Money Rehab, ARK founder and CEO Cathie Wood told Nicole Lapin exactly why:

"Our sale was all about losing Jensen [Huang] to someone else. That company being able to take a lot of share from Nvidia."

Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO earlier this month, and Wood predicted he might land with Musk: "Elon Musk has said he'd be delighted to invite Jensen to join his team, probably to help with TeraFab."

Oops. Jensen's back at Nvidia, so that blows that whole story out of the water.

Nvidia's board voted unanimously on Nov. 23 to reinstate Huang as president and CEO, effective immediately, saying in its release that it was satisfied with "Mr. Huang's candor and ability to lead NVIDIA." Huang's own line: "I can't wait to get back to work."

Strong position getting stronger

Nvidia has about 83% of the market for the GPUs that power AI, Wood told Lapin. Even if its share slid to 38%, she said, ARK's forecast still had the stock compounding at around 25% a year for five years.

Consensus has Nvidia's normalized EPS climbing from $9.67 in the year ending January 2027 to $21.77 two years later:

What changed was a scenario ARK hadn't weighed: that Huang "could go somewhere else and attract a lot of the talent from Nvidia." Only weeks earlier, ARK had added to Nvidia because "SpaceX said that it was committing to Nvidia exclusively for its orbital data centers." With Huang helping Musk, she thought SpaceX "could basically take all of their business from Nvidia."

Of course, with Huang back at Nvidia, that scenario is off the table.
